name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Tuesday 9 July 1974

solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts, agrees with the 1 answers the paper printed

clue.text: Bash her to bits before now

blocks.note: to bash something is to hit it
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to smash a woman's belongings to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bits' looks like an anagram signal, but HER and TO are already in order: the clue simply breaks HITHERTO into pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitherto is a formal adverb meaning until this point in time, up to the present.

clue.text: Has bit inserted for riding practices

definitions.note: riding habits are clothes, but habits are also practices

indicators.note: something inserted is put inside another word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; also a horse's mouthpiece, fitting the surface

explanation.surface: A horse is fitted with a bit before going riding.
explanation.walkthrough: HA(BIT)S. A riding habit is the outfit worn on horseback, so the definition puns on two kinds of habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Habits are customary practices, and riding habits are the traditional costume worn for horse riding.

clue.text: Waterproof for Jack Gauguin at home

blocks.note: jack and tar are both old words for a sailor
Paul Gauguin, the French painter
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Rainwear is wanted for a man called Jack Gauguin while he is indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a heavy tarred canvas sheet used to keep rain off, a waterproof covering.

clue.text: Gas-pipe may wear out

blocks.note: first meaning: the pipe carrying fumes away from an engine
second meaning: to tire completely

explanation.surface: A gas pipe might become worn with use.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's tailpipe expels engine fumes, and to tire someone utterly is to drain their energy completely.

clue.text: Tiptop artist of French commerce

indicators.note: the top of a down entry is its start, so only the opening letter of the tip is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word Tip
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A first-rate painter dealing in French business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiptop' reads as excellent, but it splits as the top of 'Tip'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade is the buying and selling of goods, which is exactly what commerce means.

clue.text: Repeater ammunition from Indian camp

blocks.note: first meaning: an expanding bullet, and the word itself repeats a syllable
second meaning: ..., a cantonment and arsenal near Calcutta where the bullet was first made

explanation.surface: Bullets for a repeating rifle are supplied by an army base in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeater' does double duty: a repeating rifle, and a word made of one syllable said twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumdum is a soft-nosed bullet that expands on impact, named after the Indian arsenal town where it originated.

clue.text: .Jack Sprat's fat? Not so by his wife

definitions.text: .Jack Sprat's fat? Not so by his wife

blocks.note: surface reading: the nursery rhyme in which Jack Sprat could eat no fat
setter's reading: his wife could eat no lean, so she finished the fat he left on the plate

explanation.surface: A question about the nursery rhyme couple who shared their dinner between them.
explanation.walkthrough: In the rhyme Jack Sprat could eat no fat and his wife could eat no lean, so the fat he left was not left by her.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that remains on the plate untouched is left over; Jack's fat stayed so only until his wife ate it.

clue.text: Leave has first to expire for this saint

indicators.note: having something first puts that piece at the front of the other

blocks.note: to expire is to die
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: Someone may leave, but must die first, to reach this saint.
explanation.walkthrough: Diego is Spanish for James, as in the city of San Diego.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Diego of Alcalá is a Spanish Franciscan saint, after whom the Californian city San Diego is named.

clue.text: Bed can ruin coiffure

blocks.note: to mat hair is to tangle it into a ruined mess
a tress is a lock of hair, a hairdo

explanation.surface: Sleeping on a pillow can wreck a careful hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress is the padded part of a bed you sleep on, standing for the whole bed.

clue.text: Chooses to stop pain that's troublesome

indicators.note: something troublesome is unruly and disordered, so these letters are put out of order

blocks.note: the eight letters of the two words rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone selects a way to end an ache that is bothering them.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint is to choose and name someone formally for a job or office.

clue.text: Annual salute to commemorate Colonel's arrival?

definitions.text: Annual salute to commemorate Colonel's arrival?

blocks.clueFragment: Annual salute to commemorate Colonel's arrival?
blocks.note: surface reading: a yearly military salute marking an officer's coming to a base

blocks.clueFragment: Annual salute to commemorate Colonel's arrival?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a yearly gift marking the day the Colonel arrived in the world, that is, was born

explanation.surface: A regiment fires a yearly salute to mark the day its colonel arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrival' means birth, and a 'salute' can be any tribute, such as a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift given every year on the anniversary of someone's birth is a yearly tribute to that arrival.

clue.text: Art backs dictator? Slander!

indicators.note: to back is to go in reverse, so the preceding word is read from its end

blocks.note: taken as written
Il Duce was the title of Mussolini, Italy's fascist dictator

explanation.surface: Accusing art of supporting a tyrant is called a libel.
explanation.definitionFit: To traduce someone is to speak badly and falsely of them, to defame them.

clue.text: Excel or get no income?

definitions.note: a cryptic phrase for an adjective: out of doors, where nothing comes in

blocks.note: to excel is to surpass, to outdo
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question of whether to do brilliantly or earn nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a pun: 'income' read as 'in-come', so with no coming in you stay out of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor describes life outside buildings, never coming in, punningly expressed as getting no in-come.

clue.text: Untidy girl spills salt, gets the bird

indicators.note: spilt grains scatter and land jumbled, so these letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A messy girl knocks over the salt cellar and is then attacked by a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Slattern is an old, unkind word for a woman who is dirty and careless in dress and housekeeping.

clue.text: Poor types lie about architectural feature

indicators.note: poor work is badly made, suggesting letters put together wrongly

blocks.note: the eight letters of the two words rearranged

explanation.surface: Low-quality people tell untruths about a detail of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistyle is the beam resting on top of classical columns, also called the architrave.

clue.text: Records cash at bottom of page

blocks.note: first meaning: written jottings made to remember something
second meaning: banknotes
third meaning: footnotes printed below the text

explanation.surface: An accountant enters the cash figures at the foot of a page.
explanation.walkthrough: There are really three meanings here: jottings, paper money, and footnotes at the bottom of a page.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun covers written memoranda, paper banknotes, and annotations printed beneath a page of text.

clue.text: Diplomacy needed here in France with an army commander?

definitions.note: a commander skilled in tactics; the question mark flags a definition by example

blocks.note: tact is diplomacy in dealing with people
ici is French for here
taken as written

explanation.surface: A general serving in France needs diplomatic skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactician plans manoeuvres skilfully, which is what a battlefield leader of troops must do.

clue.text: A fifty-fifty entitlement is OK

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, and there are two of them
a right is an entitlement

explanation.surface: An equal share in something is judged to be fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fifty-fifty' reads as an even split, but it is two Roman fifties.
explanation.definitionFit: All right is a phrase of approval meaning acceptable or satisfactory, the same as okay.

clue.text: Free, unattached knight lacks fortune

definitions.note: LANCE completes 'free' as freelance, meaning unattached

indicators.note: something that lacks a part is missing it, so that part is taken away

blocks.note: Sir Lancelot, a knight of King Arthur's Round Table
one's lot is one's fortune or fate

explanation.surface: A wandering knight with no lord to serve has no money either.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works with the word before it: a free lance was a mercenary knight with no lord, and freelance now means unattached to any employer.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval free lance was a mercenary knight serving no lord, the origin of freelance meaning self-employed, unbound.

clue.text: Do photographic work free

blocks.note: first meaning: to make a bigger print from a negative
second meaning, archaic: to set a prisoner at large

explanation.surface: Doing camera work without charging for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like unpaid, but it is an old sense of the verb: to release from custody.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers blow up prints to bigger sizes, and in older English to set at large meant to release a captive.

clue.text: Fashionable posture for example

blocks.note: what is in is in fashion
a stance is a way of standing, a posture

explanation.surface: A trendy way of standing is offered as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case cited as an illustration, as in the phrase for instance.

clue.text: One of the objects of apprenticeship

blocks.note: first meaning: a single item or thing
second meaning: the binding contract of a trainee

explanation.surface: A statement about one of the aims of training as an apprentice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objects' looks like aims, but means things; a trainee lawyer or tradesman was bound by articles.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is a single item, and articles were the written agreement binding an apprentice to a master.

clue.text: Scottish child journalist is on the bottle

definitions.note: describes a baby moved from breast to bottle

blocks.note: wean is Scots for a small child
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A young Scottish reporter has taken to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the bottle' suggests heavy drinking, but here it is a baby's feeding bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby taken off breast milk has been moved to other feeding, such as formula from a bottle.

clue.text: Lock for telephone — an added hindrance

blocks.note: to ring someone is to telephone them
a let is an old word for an obstruction, kept in the phrase without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: Someone finds a lock on the telephone gets in the way of calling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' looks like a door fitting, but it is a curl of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a long spiral curl of hair, and a lock is a tress or strand of hair.

clue.text: Silk for Mile de Lenclos

blocks.note: first meaning: a sheer lightweight silk or rayon fabric
second meaning: the first name of the famous seventeenth-century French courtesan and wit

explanation.surface: A silk garment chosen for a French lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a fine voile fabric, and Ninon de Lenclos was a celebrated Parisian salon hostess.

clue.text: Young Lady of Riga somewhat chilly?

blocks.note: a Lett is a Latvian, and Riga is the Latvian capital
ice is what something rather cold turns to

explanation.surface: A question about whether a young woman from Riga is a little cold in manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettice is an old-fashioned English girl's first name, so any young lady might bear it.

clue.text: I call out the time for musical show

definitions.note: the answer is what remains of the show's title

indicators.note: to call out is to summon away, so the named words are removed

blocks.note: Lilac Time, a 1922 operetta built on Schubert's melodies
taken as written, without the article

explanation.surface: Someone announces the hour at which a musical begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the operetta Lilac Time and remove its last word to leave the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac Time, minus its last word, leaves the name of the fragrant spring-flowering shrub.

clue.text: Democratic procedure for military promotion?

blocks.note: first meaning: a national vote choosing a new parliament
second meaning, whimsically: choosing an officer to be made a general

explanation.surface: A voting process used to decide army promotions.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: an election of a general.
explanation.definitionFit: A nationwide poll for all seats in parliament is the central democratic process, and could jokingly mean picking generals.

clue.text: Tom Snout to repair Peter's bell

blocks.note: first meaning: Tom Snout's trade in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream
second meaning: to mend in a fiddling, amateur way
third meaning: the fairy companion of Peter Pan is ... Bell

explanation.surface: A man called Tom Snout is asked to fix the bell belonging to Peter.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings: a Shakespeare mechanical's trade, a verb for mending, and the first half of Tinker Bell, the fairy in Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Snout is a mender of pots in the play, and to tinker is to make small amateur repairs.

clue.text: Publicly shown to be concealed

blocks.note: first meaning: broadcast or projected for an audience, as a film
second meaning: hidden behind a partition

explanation.surface: Something exhibited in public turns out to be hidden after all.
explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are near opposites, which is the joke of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A film is projected onto a cinema surface for viewers, while a partition hides whatever stands behind it.
